question: Which home feature is NOT necessary to ensure a safe and hygienic delivery space?

options.A: A clean space for the birth
options.B: A large television set for entertainment
options.C: Good lighting in the room
options.D: Access to clean running water

explanation: A television is not needed for clinical safety, whereas water, lighting, and cleanliness are essential. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is a strict safety rule for a patient being discharged after receiving sedation for an endoscopy?

options.A: They must have a responsible adult escort to take them home.
options.B: They must sign a new consent form before leaving the clinic.
options.C: They must stay in the hospital ward for at least three days.
options.D: They must avoid eating solid food for an entire week.

explanation: Because sedatives stay in the system for hours, patients are not allowed to go home alone or drive themselves. They need a trusted companion! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h8)

question: A patient with advanced, progressive cancer is admitted for rehab. Which goal makes the most sense?

options.A: Maximizing comfort and dignity
options.B: Reversing all chemotherapy side effects
options.C: Restoring pre-treatment athletic ability
options.D: Preventing future tumor growth

explanation: When the disease is advanced, our main priority shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, peaceful, and full of dignity. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h2)

question: You're teaching a patient how to get complete protein from plant sources. Which local food combination should you recommend?

options.A: Yam and palm oil
options.B: Beans and maize
options.C: Cassava and water
options.D: Plantain and salt

explanation: Brilliant! Pairing legumes like beans with a cereal like maize matches up their amino acids to give you a complete, high-quality protein. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T007#GNS227_U3_T007_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing regular skin self-examinations?

options.A: Detecting skin abnormalities at an early, treatable stage
options.B: Restoring lost moisture to severely dry epidermal layers
options.C: Completely preventing any future skin injuries from occurring
options.D: Eliminating the need for daily hygiene and moisturizing

explanation: Spot on! Catching skin changes early means any issues can be treated quickly before they turn into something serious. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h6)

question: In Nigeria, which animal is the main reservoir for the Lassa fever virus?

options.A: Stray domestic dogs
options.B: The multimammate rat
options.C: Domestic dairy cattle
options.D: Migratory waterfowl

explanation: Correct! The multimammate rat is the primary natural reservoir for Lassa fever, shedding the virus in its urine and droppings. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h4)

question: What is the best way for community health nurses to help stop unsafe abortions?

options.A: Reporting patients who come in with abortion complications
options.B: Increasing police patrols around illegal clinics
options.C: Promoting education and easy access to family planning
options.D: Banning the sale of common pain relievers

explanation: Stopping unintended pregnancies before they happen through education and contraception is the absolute best way to beat unsafe abortion. Well reasoned! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h7)

question: What early symptom is typically caused by a tumor in the head of the pancreas blocking the bile duct?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Constipation
options.D: Vision loss

explanation: You're crushing it! When a tumor blocks the bile duct, bilirubin backs up into the bloodstream, turning the skin and eyes yellow (jaundice). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the main reason a doctor would order an EEG test?

options.A: Locating tumors in the spinal column
options.B: Diagnosing and evaluating seizure disorders
options.C: Detecting blockages in carotid arteries
options.D: Measuring pressure inside the eye chambers

explanation: EEGs are most commonly used to catch those tricky abnormal electrical patterns linked with epilepsy and seizures. Super important clinical tool! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h2)

question: At what level does management happen in a hospital?

options.A: Only at the executive board room level
options.B: Exclusively within the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: At every level from charge nurse to director
options.D: Strictly during annual government audits

explanation: Management isn't just for bosses in suits! From frontline charge nurses managing the ward to senior directors, everyone plays a leadership role. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h1)

question: How does a demand pacemaker operate during a normal heart rhythm?

options.A: It pumps extra blood to compensate for the fast natural rhythm
options.B: It shuts down completely and must be manually restarted by a doctor
options.C: It continuously sends rapid shocks to speed up the normal heartbeat
options.D: It remains idle and only fires when the natural heart rate drops too low

explanation: Demand pacemakers monitor the heart's natural electrical signals and only step in when the rate falls below the programmed threshold. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which scenario best demonstrates the function of sensory association areas?

options.A: Recognizing a hot cup of tea by its steam, warmth, and aroma together
options.B: Feeling a sharp pinprick on the skin and pulling the hand away quickly
options.C: Hearing a loud sudden sound and turning the head toward the noise
options.D: Blinking automatically when a bright light flashes in front of the eyes

explanation: Recognizing an object by combining multiple sensory cues like sight, temperature, and smell requires sensory association areas. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to combine certain azoles with blood thinners like warfarin?

options.A: Warfarin destroys the chemical structure of azoles in the bloodstream
options.B: Both drugs together instantly destroy the red blood cell count
options.C: Azoles block warfarin from entering the kidneys for excretion
options.D: Azoles inhibit liver enzymes, causing warfarin levels to rise dangerously

explanation: Spot on! Azoles slow down the liver enzymes that break down warfarin. This causes warfarin to build up in the blood, vastly increasing bleeding risks. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h6)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used for animals, while quarantine is used only for humans
options.B: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.C: Isolation is done at home, while quarantine is done in a laboratory
options.D: Quarantine requires heavy medication, while isolation requires only rest

explanation: Isolation keeps confirmed infectious patients away from others, whereas quarantine watches people who might have caught the disease during their incubation period. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is a key difference between benign and malignant tumors?

options.A: Malignant tumors stay completely contained within a capsule
options.B: Malignant tumors never grow back after simple removal
options.C: Benign tumors do not spread to distant parts of the body
options.D: Benign tumors always require immediate chemotherapy

explanation: A great way to remember this in the wards is that benign tumors stay put and grow slowly. Malignant tumors are the ones that can invade other tissues and spread around. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which two bacteria are the most common and serious causes of newborn eye infections?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli
options.B: Herpes simplex virus and Candida albicans
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Brilliant! These two bugs are usually passed from mother to baby and cause the toughest eye infections. Knowing them helps you stay alert in the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h2)

question: Why do patients sometimes resist following a nursing care plan?

options.A: Fear, misunderstanding, or a perceived loss of personal control
options.B: An excessive desire to follow medical instructions perfectly
options.C: Complete agreement with the community nurse
options.D: Too much free time available during the day

explanation: Resistance is usually just fear or a worry that they are losing their independence. Once you understand that, it's easier to help them! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h6)

question: Which emergency medication is given during cardiac arrest to narrow blood vessels and boost blood pressure?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Amiodarone
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver; it squeezes peripheral blood vessels so blood gets pushed right where it's needed most: the brain and the heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient takes too much of an opioid pain medication and their breathing drops to just 4 breaths per minute. Why does this happen?

options.A: Cerebral cortex voluntarily suppressing the urge to breathe
options.B: Peripheral muscles failing to respond to normal nerve signals
options.C: Medullary respiratory centres suppressed by circulating drug molecules
options.D: Carotid baroreceptors shutting off blood flow to the lungs

explanation: Opioids can bind to the brainstem and quiet down the breathing center so much that it forgets to signal the body to breathe at a normal rate. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T14#GNS211_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which tiny structures form right next to the neural tube in an embryo to eventually build our skeletal muscles?

options.A: Somites
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Lateral plate mesoderm
options.D: Pharyngeal arches

explanation: Somites are little blocks of tissue that line up next to the neural tube and develop into our skeletal muscles and bones. Great job learning the building blocks of the body! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the most important daily protection for a leprosy patient whose feet have lost feeling?

options.A: Soaking the feet in hot water daily to stimulate blood flow
options.B: Applying strong chemical antiseptics to unbroken skin daily
options.C: Wearing well-fitted, protective footwear at all times
options.D: Binding the toes tightly together to prevent accidental stubbing

explanation: Spot on! Since they can't feel pain, good shoes protect their soles from everyday cuts, stones, and ulcers. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of giving medications directly as eye or ear drops instead of pills?

options.A: It stops the patient from blinking too much during the day
options.B: It completely removes the need for nursing assessments
options.C: It keeps the drug working locally and prevents unwanted body-wide side effects
options.D: It ensures the drug goes straight to the liver for activation

explanation: Spot-on! Using drops means the medicine stays right where it's needed in the eye or ear, without floating all around the rest of the body causing side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of conducting regular nursing documentation audits in a health facility?

options.A: To find reasons to suspend nurses who make minor spelling mistakes
options.B: To collect extra money from clients during home visits
options.C: To evaluate the quality of care and ensure compliance with professional standards
options.D: To reduce the number of clients admitted to the community program

explanation: Audits help identify gaps in clinical practice and documentation, guiding continuous quality improvement in patient care. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)

question: What is the best way to stop a nasogastric tube from getting blocked?

options.A: Changing the tube to a smaller size every week
options.B: Adding cooking oil to every feed
options.C: Flushing it with warm water before and after feeds and drugs
options.D: Blowing air down the tube twice a shift

explanation: Regular water flushes wash away sticky food and medicine residue before they can dry up and clog your tube. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the medical term for excessive thirst experienced by a client with high blood sugar?

options.A: Proteinuria
options.B: Polyuria
options.C: Polyphagia
options.D: Polydipsia

explanation: Polydipsia is the medical word for extreme thirst, which happens because the body loses a lot of water through frequent urination. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions in clinical practice?

options.A: Whenever a patient displays symptoms of an active fever
options.B: Exclusively in intensive care units and surgical theaters
options.C: Only when caring for patients with confirmed airborne diseases
options.D: For all patients receiving care, regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions are the baseline level of infection control used for every single patient interaction to prevent blood and fluid exposure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: What makes a home-based care plan different from a hospital care plan?

options.A: It focuses only on physical ailments and ignores mental health
options.B: It relies entirely on high-tech electronic equipment
options.C: It must fit the everyday resources and lifestyle of the family
options.D: It is written by the family members without professional input

explanation: Home care plans must be practical and realistic for the client's home environment to ensure lasting success. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is psychosocial support so important in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: To teach residents advanced corporate business management
options.B: To help residents cope with the mental trauma of displacement and loss
options.C: To replace the need for clean drinking water
options.D: To make sure people follow commercial tax rules

explanation: Spot on! Losing your home and community causes deep emotional pain. Mental health and psychosocial support are crucial for true healing and recovery. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h7)

question: Why should nurses encourage elderly residents to do parts of their own bath and hygiene care?

options.A: To preserve their dignity and functional independence
options.B: To lower the financial cost of facility operations
options.C: To eliminate the need for any assistive devices
options.D: To reduce the workload of the nursing staff completely

explanation: You got it! Doing things for themselves—even small tasks—helps residents keep their strength and feel good about their independence. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T1#GNS324_U5_T1_h4)

question: What actually makes air rush into your lungs when you take an inhalation?

options.A: Intrapulmonary pressure drops below atmospheric pressure
options.B: Surfactant expands the alveolar volume rapidly
options.C: Atmospheric pressure drops below intrapulmonary pressure
options.D: The diaphragm relaxes and pushes the chest upward

explanation: You nailed it! When your chest gets bigger, the pressure inside drops lower than the outside air, sucking air naturally right in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h4)

question: When does the postpartum period officially begin?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: Twenty-four hours after delivery
options.C: When the baby takes its first breath
options.D: At the start of labor

explanation: The postnatal period kicks off right after the third stage of labor when the placenta comes out. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h1)

question: What is an aortic aneurysm?

options.A: A complete blockage of a vein by a clot
options.B: An abnormal ballooning or weak bulge in the wall of an artery
options.C: A sudden cramp in the heart arteries during stress
options.D: Inflammation of the surface veins in the calf

explanation: An aneurysm happens when a weak spot in a major artery wall starts to stretch and balloon outward, kind of like a weak spot on an old bicycle inner tube. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why do many victims of abusive widowhood rites keep quiet instead of reporting the abusers to the police?

options.A: Police stations are legally prohibited from entering rural towns
options.B: Widows automatically lose all rights to vote if they file a report
options.C: Traditional laws always supersede federal laws in Nigerian courts
options.D: Fear of community ostracization and lack of legal awareness

explanation: Social pressure, fear of being rejected by their people, and not knowing their legal rights stop many women from speaking out. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T10#GNS225_U6_T10_h4)

question: How do A-delta nerve fibers behave differently from C nerve fibers?

options.A: A-delta fibers only react to emotional stress
options.B: A-delta fibers only work inside the brain and spinal cord
options.C: A-delta fibers carry dull aches over a long time
options.D: A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin and carry sharp pain very quickly

explanation: Because A-delta fibers have a protective coating (myelin), they rush the message to your brain, giving you that immediate sharp sting right when you get hurt. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which bloodborne virus is known to survive on environmental surfaces for several days?

options.A: Ebola Virus
options.B: Rabies Virus
options.C: Hepatitis B Virus
options.D: Human Immunodeficiency Virus

explanation: Good job! Hepatitis B is remarkably hardy and can stay infectious on surfaces outside the body for quite a while, which is why strict disinfection matters so much. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h4)

question: What do we call citizens who are forced to leave their homes because of conflicts or floods?

options.A: Orphans and Vulnerable Children
options.B: Internally Displaced Persons
options.C: Persons with Disabilities
options.D: Corporate health executives

explanation: When people are forced to flee within their own country (IDPs), they often live in temporary camps and rely heavily on special community health outreaches. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T27#GNS225_U5_T27_h2)

question: A patient says they take a blood pressure pill every morning. What crucial detail is still missing?

options.A: The name of the pharmacy that sold it
options.B: The color of the box the pills come in
options.C: The exact dosage strength of the pill
options.D: The weather on the day they started it

explanation: Knowing the drug name is good, but without the specific dose, you cannot assess safety or give correct care. You are thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h3)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Filtering waste and storing urine
options.B: Producing red blood cells and digesting fats
options.C: Producing gametes and secreting sex hormones
options.D: Manufacturing mucus and housing fetal tissue

explanation: The ovaries create egg cells and release hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main reason we write an incident report in the hospital?

options.A: To provide a permanent record for police investigations
options.B: To lower hospital insurance payments after a lawsuit
options.C: To gather evidence to sack a careless staff member
options.D: To document unexpected events and improve patient safety

explanation: Spot on! Incident reports are all about catching system errors so we can prevent them from happening again—not for witch-hunting or punishing staff. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h1)

question: You check an IV site and notice it is swollen, cool to the touch, and painful while the pump is running. What's happening?

options.A: An air bubble has triggered the internal line sensor
options.B: The medication is working at its optimal therapeutic level
options.C: The pump battery is failing and needs to be replaced
options.D: Fluid has leaked into the surrounding tissue (infiltration)

explanation: Spot on! Cool, swollen, and painful tissue around the site means the fluid is going into the arm tissue instead of the vein. Time to stop the infusion and restart! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which set of findings represents standard vital signs taken during a routine check?

options.A: Vision score, hearing clarity, and skin moisture
options.B: Height, weight, shoe size, and blood glucose level
options.C: Muscle strength, reflex speed, and joint flexibility
options.D: Temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure

explanation: These four measurements track core body functions and are universally tracked as primary vital signs. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: In ventilator settings, what does the acronym PEEP stand for?

options.A: Peak External Exhalational Parameter
options.B: Pulmonary End-Ejection Pressure
options.C: Positive End-Expiratory Pressure
options.D: Primary Expiratory Expansion Protocol

explanation: PEEP keeps a tiny bit of pressure in the tiny air sacs (alveoli) at the very end of a breath so they don't collapse on themselves. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h3)

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system does community health nursing support the most?

options.A: Primary health care
options.B: International health agencies
options.C: Private specialist care
options.D: Tertiary healthcare

explanation: You nailed it! Community health nurses work right at the grassroots level, which is the solid foundation of primary health care in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h8)

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?

options.A: Immunization, Environment, and Community
options.B: Information, Education, and Communication
options.C: Infection Eradication and Control
options.D: Illness Evaluation and Clinical care

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are the foundational pillars of public health messaging and community health promotion. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does a person feel breathless when there is a mismatch in breathing signals?

options.A: The brain gets confused because the effort of trying to breathe doesn't match how the lungs actually move.
options.B: The brainstem shuts down ventilation to conserve oxygen.
options.C: The diaphragm relaxes completely and refuses to contract further.
options.D: The heart pumps too much blood to the lungs, causing fluid overload.

explanation: Breathlessness happens when the brain's command to breathe doesn't match the actual movement of the chest wall. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why should a nurse manager mix and match different motivational theories on the ward?

options.A: Different nurses have unique professional needs and career drivers
options.B: Only one theory applies to nurses working night shifts
options.C: Using a single theory is illegal under labor laws
options.D: Hospital accreditation boards require all theories to be used equally

explanation: Spot on! Every nurse is different. What motivates a fresh graduate might be totally different from what drives a senior nursing officer. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is it often hard to convince patients to take their blood pressure pills every single day?

options.A: Antihypertensive drugs taste extremely sweet.
options.B: Blood pressure medications only work during the rainy season.
options.C: Pills are too large to swallow comfortably.
options.D: Patients often feel fine and may not see the need to take drugs daily.

explanation: Spot on! Because high blood pressure usually doesn't make people feel sick day-to-day, they might mistakenly think they don't need their meds. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which specific protein in the intestine makes Oral Rehydration Therapy work so well?

options.A: SGLT1
options.B: Gastric lipase
options.C: Potassium pump
options.D: Insulin receptor

explanation: SGLT1 (sodium-glucose linked transporter type 1) is the hero protein! It links sugar and salt uptake in the small intestine to pull precious water into the body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h3)

question: Which type of questioning helps an anxious PAC patient share their story comfortably?

options.A: Closed yes-or-no prompts
options.B: Open-ended questions
options.C: Leading legal inquiries
options.D: Rapid fire interrogation

explanation: Asking questions like 'How have you been feeling since yesterday?' lets patients talk in their own words without feeling cornered. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of a Root Cause Analysis after a serious medical error?

options.A: Finding which specific nurse to terminate immediately
options.B: Writing a public apology letter for the newspaper
options.C: Calculating the financial lawsuit settlement amount
options.D: Discovering the underlying systemic factors that caused the error

explanation: RCA looks beyond the individual worker to examine flawed processes, equipment, and environment factors that permitted the mistake. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy on a thyroid lump?

options.A: To obtain cells for microscopic examination to check for cancer
options.B: To inject radioactive isotopes directly into the thyroid tissue
options.C: To completely remove the entire thyroid gland without surgery
options.D: To measure the 24-hour baseline hormone production levels

explanation: Spot on! An FNA takes a tiny sample of cells so the lab can check them under a microscope to confirm or rule out cancer. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is a major advantage of breast milk over animal milk for a newborn?

options.A: It has a much higher concentration of heavy proteins
options.B: It contains protective antibodies that fight off infections
options.C: It requires no digestion by the infant's stomach
options.D: It stays fresh at room temperature for days

explanation: Breast milk is nature's vaccine! It's packed with antibodies that protect a newborn's delicate immune system against germs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h2)

question: Which activity is a great example of 'organizing' on a clinical ward?

options.A: Disciplining a staff member for arriving late
options.B: Ensuring dressing carts are fully stocked and placed near patient rooms
options.C: Deciding the long-term budget goals for the hospital
options.D: Giving a motivational speech during morning handover

explanation: Stocking and positioning your gear ahead of time is classic organizing that makes clinical work a breeze. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why must physical patient registers and folders be locked away in storage cabinets when not in use?

options.A: It stops government auditors from reviewing financial records.
options.B: It protects sensitive client information from unauthorized access and maintains privacy.
options.C: It ensures nurses spend more time looking for missing keys.
options.D: It prevents facility rodents from chewing on paper pages.

explanation: Locking records away keeps prying eyes off private medical history and honors our professional duty of confidentiality. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h8)

question: Why do nurses check routine blood tests for medical-surgical patients?

options.A: To replace the need for physical head-to-toe assessments
options.B: To permanently cure chronic underlying disease processes
options.C: To measure the exact total volume of blood in the body
options.D: To monitor physiological shifts and evaluate organ function

explanation: Blood tests are like a window into the body! They give you clear clues on how well internal organs are coping, helping you track your patient's recovery day by day. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why can relying completely on international donors be risky for a hospital's Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: International agencies refuse to supply common medicines like antibiotics
options.B: Donor drugs are always expired before they arrive at the hospital
options.C: Local nurses are legally forbidden from handling donated medical items
options.D: Donor programs can end or shift priorities abruptly, causing shortages

explanation: Right! External aid can disappear overnight. If you don't have a local system making money to buy drugs, you'll run out fast when donors leave. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h5)

question: You notice local food vendors leaving cooked rice uncovered in an open market stall. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Provide practical education on food protection and cover methods
options.B: Close down all food businesses in the region permanently
options.C: Imprison the vendors without warning or explanation
options.D: Ignore the practice since it is a traditional custom

explanation: Fantastic nursing judgment! As public health nurses, our first superpower is education. Always teach and guide before jumping to harsh punishments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h6)

question: What is the main responsibility of the supplementary motor area (SMA)?

options.A: Regulating baseline heart rate and breathing
options.B: Processing sharp pain and temperature sensations
options.C: Planning and sequencing complex movements
options.D: Translating spoken words into written text

explanation: You've got this! The SMA acts like a master planner, organizing movement sequences before you actually perform them. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why do youth health programmes include counseling against substance abuse?

options.A: Substance use is a legal matter handled exclusively by police officers.
options.B: Alcohol and drugs are only used by teenagers.
options.C: Lifestyle habits formed during youth heavily influence long-term health outcomes.
options.D: It is a requirement to receive government funding for equipment.

explanation: Spot on! Habits picked up in the teenage years often stick around. Catching substance use early helps prevent lifelong health struggles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h4)

question: Why do women need to use chemical spermicide along with a diaphragm?

options.A: To lubricate the device for easy insertion
options.B: To immobilize and kill sperm that pass the barrier

explanation: Spot on! The cornea is that clear, curved window at the front of the eye that does the heavy lifting of bending light rays before they even reach the lens. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of the Circle of Willis at the base of the brain?

options.A: To drain deoxygenated blood away from the cerebral cortex
options.B: To cool down the blood before it reaches delicate brain tissue
options.C: To provide alternative blood supply routes if a vessel is blocked
options.D: To produce cerebrospinal fluid for the central nervous system

explanation: Spot on! The Circle of Willis acts like a backup traffic network. If one path gets blocked, it reroutes blood so the brain keeps getting what it needs. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h1)

question: A patient is getting intravenous Amphotericin B for a severe kidney fungal infection. Which lab tests should you check most closely?

options.A: Platelet count and bleeding time
options.B: Liver enzymes and bilirubin levels
options.C: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.D: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen

explanation: Because Amphotericin B is harsh on the kidneys, we always monitor kidney function markers like creatinine and BUN closely. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h3)

question: What does giving 'holistic nursing care' mean?

options.A: Exclusively treating the biological cause of the acute disease
options.B: The physical, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions of the client
options.C: Strictly checking the financial cost of prescribed drugs
options.D: Only looking at physical lab test results on the chart

explanation: Fantastic! Holistic care means treating the whole person—body, mind, emotions, and spirit, not just a disease. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is preparing a patient for common drug side effects an important counselling objective?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will never return again
options.B: It allows the patient to sell extra doses to others safely
options.C: It prevents patients from panicking and stopping treatment early
options.D: It eliminates all biological reactions to the medication

explanation: When patients know what mild side effects to expect, they are less likely to abandon their prescription out of fear. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the most common cause of sore and cracked nipples in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Natural thinning of the skin during pregnancy
options.B: Drinking too little water during the day
options.C: Excessive washing of the breasts with soap
options.D: Improper latch and attachment technique

explanation: When a baby only takes the nipple instead of a large part of the areola, friction causes pain and tissue breakdown. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: Why is resource management often tough in public Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: Hospitals have excess funds that are difficult to spend before the year ends
options.B: There are too many nurses available for every single hospital bed
options.C: Financial resources and medical supplies are often limited compared to the patient load
options.D: Patients refuse to use any medications provided by the government

explanation: When funds and supplies are tight compared to the heavy number of patients, nurse managers have to be very smart about prioritizing. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving a patient a new biological medication?

options.A: Ensuring the medication is stored in direct sunlight at room temperature
options.B: Crushing the vial contents into water for oral intake
options.C: Assuming all biological products are completely safe from side effects
options.D: Watching the patient closely for any signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Because biological and animal-based drugs carry a higher risk of triggering the immune system, keeping a close eye on your patient is a must. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h8)

question: When someone takes an NSAID like ibuprofen for a headache, which chemical messenger is blocked to stop the pain and swelling?

options.A: Adrenaline
options.B: Prostaglandins
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Histamines

explanation: Think of prostaglandins as the body's local alarm chemicals that trigger pain and swelling. NSAIDs block the enzymes that make them, giving you sweet relief! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Diabetes mellitus
options.B: Drinking adequate water
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Eating fresh fruits daily

explanation: Chronic conditions like diabetes damage blood vessels and nerves over time, making it a major physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h3)

question: A nurse wants to document the exact number of malaria cases in a clinic last month. Which study type fits best?

options.A: Experimental laboratory design
options.B: Descriptive design
options.C: Explanatory design
options.D: Exploratory design

explanation: Correct! When you are just describing what is happening naturally without testing causes, it's a descriptive study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h4)

question: At what point should waste sorting (segregation) happen in the clinical ward?

options.A: At the end of the nursing shift
options.B: When the cleaner arrives with large trucks
options.C: After the waste reaches the municipal dump
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right where you use it prevents dangerous mix-ups and keeps everyone handling it safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: When you suspect a notifiable disease, what patient detail is MOST critical to record?

options.A: Patient's favorite food and dietary preferences
options.B: The brand of soap used in the patient's household
options.C: Patient's correct address and contact information
options.D: The specific color of the patient's bedsheets

explanation: Exactly! Public health officers need a correct address and phone number so they can find the patient and trace contacts fast. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h4)
